articles.title: Shohei Ohtani bats sixth in Dodgers' NLCS Game 3 lineup, his lowest start since 2020
articles.summary: Ohtani is 1-for-7 through two games of the NLCS.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts promised Tuesday that Shohei Ohtani would remain in the team's lineup for Game 3 of the NLCS on Wednesday against the Milwaukee Brewers.

The lineup was released Wednesday afternoon, and it showed Ohtani batting sixth — the lowest he has ever appeared in the batting order during his time with the Dodgers.

Ohtani will follow Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman, Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Andy Pages. He'll bat ahead of Will Smith, Miguel Rojas and Tommy Edman.

Roberts said after his team's loss in Game 2 that they would discuss what is best for Ohtani, as the slugger is just 1-for-7 at the plate in the series while fighting through knee and biceps injuries. The Milwaukee Brewers lead the series 2-0.

"Yeah, I mean, obviously, it hasn't been good. He doesn't feel great. I think for me, it's having a conversation with him tomorrow, kind of try to figure out what's best for him, what's best for us. He certainly has earned that conversation and deserves it. "I'll have [that conversation] with him tomorrow."

"Yeah, I mean, obviously, it hasn't been good. He doesn't feel great. I think for me, it's having a conversation with him tomorrow, kind of try to figure out what's best for him, what's best for us. He certainly has earned that conversation and deserves it.

"I'll have [that conversation] with him tomorrow."

Ohtani reportedly said he was "very convicted" about improving and "adamant" he feels good enough to play, per MLB.com's Sonja Chen .

Following Roberts' announcement, the designated hitter spoke to the media through interpreter Will Ireton . He said, in part, "I take full responsibility. … The symptoms shouldn't be the reason why I can't hit."

Ohtani spoke about how his injuries have improved. "The symptoms have subdued a lot, especially when I was on the IL," he said. "As of now, the swing is a daily process of trying different things."

Ohtani's struggles have not been limited to this series. He's 3-for-20 with three walks and seven strikeouts in the postseason. He hasn't registered an extra-base hit, as all three of his hits have been singles. Over his six postseason games so far, he is slashing just .150/.261/.150.

The Dodgers slugger missed much of the final month of the regular season due to knee and biceps injuries. Since Aug. 14, he slashed .198/.305/.363 in his final 23 regular-season games.

Ohtani was added to the IL in September and didn't play from Sept. 9 to Sept. 23. When he was activated, he was still dealing with issues. He admitted ahead of the NLDS against the Atlanta Braves that he would need to " manage " both injuries through the playoffs.

The Dodgers' designated hitter hit fourth in the series opener but then was dropped to fifth in the order for Game 2 — his lowest start in the batting order since 2020 with the L.A. Angels.

The NLCS is a best-of-seven series. Game 3 is Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET in Los Angeles.

articles.title: Astros’ 4 best Joe Espada manager replacements
articles.summary: The Houston Astros are officially searching for a new manager after deciding not to renew Joe Espada’s contract following three seasons at the helm. Espada h...
articles.body:
The Houston Astros are officially searching for a new manager after deciding not to renew Joe Espada 's contract following three seasons at the helm. Espada helped Houston win two American League West titles, but the team's recent postseason struggles ultimately led the organization in a different direction. Now, the Astros must identify the right person to lead a roster that still has championship aspirations but needs to prove it can compete consistently in October.

Houston has several potential options, ranging from familiar faces within the organization to experienced managers and former players looking to make the jump into the dugout. It should be noted that Omar Lopez, the current Astros bench coach, has already been offered a different role to stay with the team . While he could get an interview for the job, it seems the organization wants a new face in the building.

Here are four candidates the Astros should consider (in no particular order) as they begin their search for Espada's replacement.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Ausmus offers Houston a combination of organizational familiarity and major league managerial experience. The former Astros catcher has deep ties to the franchise and previously interviewed for the team's managerial opening before Dusty Baker was hired.

Ausmus managed the Detroit Tigers from 2014 through 2017 and the Los Angeles Angels in 2019. Those experiences give him an understanding of the responsibilities and challenges that come with leading a major league clubhouse. He has since worked as the New York Yankees' bench coach, continuing to gain experience on a staff competing under significant expectations.

Houston would be taking a calculated risk by bringing Ausmus back into the organization in a leadership role, but his background makes him a candidate. His familiarity with the franchise could help him adapt quickly.

Linares would be another appealing option for an organization that values player development and familiarity with its personnel. He spent 21 seasons in Houston's organization, managing throughout the minor leagues before joining Tampa Bay's major league coaching staff.

During his time in Houston's farm system, Linares worked with several players who became central figures in the Astros' success, including José Altuve and Carlos Correa. He now serves as the Rays' bench coach, giving him additional experience working alongside a major league manager.

Linares has not managed at the major league level, which would make his hiring a significant step. However, his extensive experience developing talent and his familiarity with Houston's organizational structure could help him establish credibility with the clubhouse.

Albert Pujols , Dominican Republic Manager

Pujols would represent a much different direction for Houston, but his name deserves consideration. The Hall of Fame slugger has expressed interest in becoming a major league manager and has already gained experience leading teams after his playing career. He managed the Dominican Republic in the 2026 World Baseball Classic and previously interviewed for the San Diego Padres' managerial opening .

Pujols would bring immediate credibility to a clubhouse filled with accomplished veterans. His playing career gives him firsthand knowledge of the pressures elite athletes face, and his leadership could resonate with established stars.

The obvious concern is his lack of major league managerial experience. Managing a national team loaded with talent is different from navigating a 162-game season, managing a pitching staff and making adjustments over several months. Still, Houston could consider Pujols if it believes his leadership and baseball knowledge outweigh the risks.

Banister would give Houston an experienced option who already understands the American League West. He managed the Texas Rangers from 2015 through 2018, won two division titles and earned American League Manager of the Year honors in 2015.

His familiarity with the division could be valuable as Houston attempts to reclaim its place among the American League's top teams. Banister also has previous connections to the Astros, having interviewed for the organization's managerial position before the team hired A.J. Hinch.

Banister has since continued his coaching career, most recently serving as the Arizona Diamondbacks' bench coach. His combination of managerial experience, division knowledge, and familiarity with Houston makes him a candidate if the Astros prefer an established leader over a first-time manager.

Ultimately, Houston's next hire must do more than maintain the status quo. The Astros need someone who can manage a demanding clubhouse, maximize the roster's talent, and help the team translate regular-season success into postseason wins. Each of these five candidates offers a different path forward, but the organization must decide which leadership style gives it the best chance to return to championship contention.
